title: John Penny, trumpeter from a tent show
summary: John Penny's career in road shows and his move to Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: He'd have been about, John Penny must have been about 69 or 70 years old when he came to work with us at the point. He came off a rabbit foot show.
I think I've heard of that. I've heard of John Pendleton.
Was he like a circus man or like a brass band?
They call it Connival. Connival. That's what they call Connival. But he had been, from what I learned, he had been with all kinds of people like Solid and all those road shows.
Yeah. Well, I'd say I never-
Yeah. I never saw many of those. I saw a few of them. But what kind of music would they play on a Tenshill? Roachill.
Tenshill plays a type of music, what you call a ballyhorn. It plays a lot of bass music.
Would there be popular songs with jazz or would there be brass bands?
More popular songs and brass bands too. Jesse Charles can tell you more about it because he was on that.
Yeah. But I just wonder what Penny played like.
Well, he's a fine trumpet player. You see, he had been playing so much show music until it took him a month to break down to Dixie.

Where was he from? I don't know where Penny was from, but he had been around Alexander, Louisiana playing with a band by the name of Harry Walker. Because all the, all the, all the new york musicians, a lot of old new york musicians knew him. He was great, great trumpet player man. Triple tongue, everything. Reed, bass reader. Fake tooth.
But he, he got back with the Dixieland. Got perfect with the Dixieland.
